newsitem.title: UK: CIA says won't overpromise on TV again.
newsitem.headline: CIA says won't overpromise on TV again.

text.p: CIA Group Plc, parent of the Cia Medianetwork planning and buying group, said on Thursday it had taken steps to ensure it would not repeat the costly mistake of promising too much to television contractors.

CIA said earlier it would pay 1.8 million pounds to settle a dispute with contractors for Britain's Independent Television Network, including Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc, Granada Group Plc, and United News & Media Plc.
"We overpromised," CIA finance director Peter Toynton told Reuters in a telephone interview. "We won't overpromise again."
Toynton said CIA had strengthened administration procedures on the TV buying side.
Yorkshire-Tyne Tees filed an 800,000 pound lawsuit against CIA Medianetwork in November for allegedly failing to deliver on promised advertising revenues.

Television sales houses, such as Granada's Laser and United News' TMSS, sell commercial airtime based on promises geared to the size of viewing audiences and/or the share of ITV revenue. Media buyers also pool advertisers' spending to obtain volume discounts.
